primary_factors: Rain/showers are forecast Sunday (11/29) with temps well above freezing, so roads could be wet going into Sunday night.

Temperatures are forecast to be right around freezing by early Monday (11/30) morning (about 32°F). That creates some risk of patchy refreeze/black ice on untreated surfaces (especially bridges/overpasses and shaded roads).

Precipitation is forecast to end before the main Monday morning bus window (NWS: showers mainly before 1 AM Sunday night; your hourly data shows precip chances dropping to ~1% after 1 AM). That keeps the icing risk lower than a true freezing-rain event.
No meaningful snow accumulation signal in the provided forecast; ordinary light/wet snow mixing in would usually be a minor travel issue by itself.
Road conditions, pavement temperatures, and whether roads dry out overnight are unknown at this time (forecast hazard, not observed conditions).
decision_rationale:
Based on the hourly forecast you provided, Sunday (11/29) features many hours of rain showers with temps mainly in the upper 30s to low 40s, then precipitation chances fall off overnight with temps trending down to about 32°F for the Monday (11/30) morning commute. That pattern can create patchy black ice if pavement stays wet and temps slip to/just below freezing before buses run, but it does not look like a widespread snowstorm or freezing-rain setup.

NWS evidence available as of the forecast issue time supports this lower-impact picture:
- NWS Point Forecast for Rockford, MI (last update shown on page: 10:03 PM EST Thu Nov 26, 2026) calls for: Sunday "Showers"; Sunday night "A 40 percent chance of showers before 1am" with a low around 32; and Monday "Partly sunny" with a high near 39. Source: `https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?CityName=Rockford&lat=43.1262&lon=-85.5566&site=GRR&state=MI` (forecast valid through Dec 3). ([forecast.weather.gov](https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?CityName=Rockford&lat=43.1262&lon=-85.5566&site=GRR&state=MI))
- NWS Grand Rapids Area Forecast Discussion (issued 12:32 PM EST Fri Nov 27, 2026) notes that Sunday night into Monday could see some snow mixing in but that accumulating snow chances look low, and states "Overall, no real impacts to travel are expected except for some wet roads at times." Source: `https://forecast.weather.gov/product.php?format=TXT&glossary=0&issuedby=GRR&product=AFD&site=NWS&version=1` (FXUS63 KGRR 271732). ([forecast.weather.gov](https://forecast.weather.gov/product.php?format=TXT&glossary=0&issuedby=GRR&product=AFD&site=NWS&version=1))

Given this, a districtwide, full-day closure on Monday is unlikely. The main thing that could still cause problems is an overnight temperature drop a few degrees colder than forecast (turning leftover water into more widespread ice) or showers lingering later and ending with temps below 32°F. Those outcomes are not the primary forecast right now, so the best estimate for a full-day closure is low (5%).
